past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The perpendicular distance between axis of rotation and the line of action of force is called
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Moment arm (or lever arm) is defined as the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation to the line of action of the force.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text:
After disturbance, if a body comes to rest and its centre of gravity remains unchanged, then this state of the body is/ are identified as
I. stable equilibrium
II. unstable equilibrium
III. neutral equilibrium
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: In neutral equilibrium, when a body is displaced, its centre of gravity remains at the same height (unchanged).

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: Let suppose, a hole is drilled through the Earth along the diametre and a stone is dropped into it. Suppose when the stone reaches the Earth’s centre keeping same size and shape, it will have constant
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Mass is an intrinsic property of matter and remains constant everywhere, including at the center of the Earth.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: A satellite is revolving around the Earth in a circular orbit with velocity v. If the gravitational force between the satellite and the Earth suddenly disappears, then the velocity of the satellite will be
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: According to Newton's first law of motion (inertia), an object in motion will continue to move at a constant velocity in a straight line unless acted upon by an external net force. If the gravitational force disappears, there is no longer a centripetal force to keep it in a circular orbit, so it will continue to move tangentially with the same velocity v.

crqs.question: State Hooke's law and define the limit of proportionality on a load–extension graph.
crqs.answer: Hooke's law states that within the limit of proportionality, the extension of a spring is directly proportional to the applied stretching force (F = kx). The limit of proportionality is the point beyond which the load–extension graph ceases to be a straight line.

erqs.question: Describe an experiment to determine the spring constant k of a helical spring and interpret the elastic limit on its load–extension curve.
erqs.answer: Suspend a helical spring vertically next to a millimetre scale, record pointer readings for incremental slotted weights, and plot Load F against Extension x. The gradient F/x in the linear region gives the spring constant k.

numericals.problem: A helical spring of unstretched length 15 cm extends to 21 cm when a load of 12 N is suspended from it. Calculate its spring constant k in N/m.
numericals.solution: Extension x = 21 cm - 15 cm = 6 cm = 0.06 m. Therefore k = 12 N / 0.06 m = 200 N/m.
